microsoft-azure-consumption-commitment.title: Azure Consumption Commitment benefit – Microsoft Marketplace – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-azure-consumption-commitment.notes: A Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment is a contractual agreement in which an organization promises to spend a defined amount on Azure over an agreed period. Under the Azure Consumption Commitment benefit, eligible purchases made through Microsoft Marketplace count automatically toward that commitment. Offers that carry the "Azure benefit eligible" badge qualify, and Azure services billed through a marketplace deployment under the Microsoft Product Terms generally count as well. For eligible offers from Microsoft partners, the full net purchase price before taxes is credited. To benefit, the organization needs a commitment agreement and an Azure subscription linked to it, and the buyer must sign in with a tenant tied to that organization. Buyers are advised to purchase in the Azure portal and use the "Get it in Azure portal" button at checkout. Limits apply: purchases funded by Azure prepayment, direct credit-card purchases in the marketplace and licenses used in hybrid or on-premises setups do not count, and agreements signed before the benefit existed may carry exclusions that the Microsoft account executive clarifies.

microsoft-certified-trainer.title: Microsoft Certified Trainer program – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-certified-trainer.notes: Microsoft Certified Trainer is an annual membership status for professionals who teach Microsoft technologies to customers. Microsoft Training Services Partners are required to have official Microsoft courseware delivered by MCTs, so the membership qualifies people to deliver that content. Members receive benefits such as software licenses, service credits and exam discounts, whose use follows the MCT Program Agreement and Microsoft licensing policies. A closed community called the MCT Lounge on the Microsoft Tech Community offers program meetings, courseware updates, discussion forums and feedback channels to Microsoft teams, and virtual or in-person events connect trainers with Microsoft staff and partners that post job offers. To join, applicants submit an online application and accept the MCT Program Agreement every year, and approved members must join the MCT Lounge. A separate Alumni program exists for trainers in good standing who no longer teach actively; it has no annual fee and keeps only lounge access and exam discounts. Specific eligibility criteria and benefit amounts are not detailed on the page itself.

microsoft-defender-easm.title: Defender External Attack Surface Management overview – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-defender-easm.notes: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management continuously discovers and maps an organization's digital attack surface and gives an outside-in view of its online infrastructure. Security and IT teams use it to find unknown assets, prioritize risks and gain control over exposures beyond the firewall. Discovery relies on proprietary Microsoft technology that recursively follows observed connections from known legitimate assets, called discovery seeds, and infers which resources belong to the organization. Asset types include domains, IP blocks, hosts, email contacts, autonomous system numbers and Whois organizations. Found assets are indexed in an inventory and classified as recent or historic, and dashboards present insights on vulnerabilities, compliance and security hygiene. The inventory can be filtered, for example for assets linked to expiring infrastructure or for new cloud resources. Owner and Contributor roles can create, edit and delete resources and assets, while Reader can only view. Cross-tenant access, including through Azure Lighthouse, is not supported, and because discovery is based on inference it is not a full guarantee of coverage. After a resource is deleted, Microsoft cannot restore it.

microsoft-graph-schema-extensions.title: schemaExtension resource type – Microsoft Graph – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-graph-schema-extensions.notes: A schema extension in Microsoft Graph defines a schema that lets an app add strongly typed custom data to a resource type. The custom data appears as a complex type on the extended resource and is managed through the same REST request as the resource itself. Supported resources include user, group, administrativeUnit, contact, device, event, message, organization and post. The definition has an id, an owner (the appId of the owning application), a status, a list of typed properties, the target types it may be applied to and a description. The id can use a verified domain name plus schema name, or an ext prefix with eight alphanumeric characters. A definition starts as InDevelopment, where only the owner can update it additively or delete it. Once set to Available, it can be used by apps in all tenants, changes stay additive and deletion is no longer possible. In the Deprecated state the definition can no longer be read or changed, although stored values can still be read, updated and deleted. Available definitions are visible to every developer, but the data created from them is tenant specific and requires explicitly granted permissions. The id and owner cannot be changed after creation.

microsoft-purview-content-search.title: Content search in Microsoft Purview – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-purview-content-search.notes: Content search is a tool in the Microsoft Purview portal for quickly finding content across Microsoft 365. It can search email in Exchange mailboxes, documents on SharePoint sites and OneDrive locations, and chat messages, including content in Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 Groups. A search is created by choosing content sources and optionally entering a keyword query; without a query, all items in the chosen locations are returned. Conditions narrow the query, and keyword statistics help refine it. Search permissions filters can limit eDiscovery managers to a subset of mailboxes or sites. The tool can also cover cloud mailboxes of users with on-premises mailboxes, imported third-party data and Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses stored in custodian mailboxes. Results can be exported, and messages can be deleted from mailboxes, for instance after a phishing attack. PowerShell scripts support targeted collections and bulk searches. Estimated and exported result counts can differ, and partially indexed items can be included or left out of an export. The page states that classic eDiscovery experiences were retired on 31 August 2025, so its guidance applies only to organizations hosted by 21Vianet in China; others should use the new eDiscovery experience.

microsoft-sentinel-data-lake.title: Microsoft Sentinel data lake overview – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-sentinel-data-lake.notes: Microsoft Sentinel data lake is a cloud-native, fully managed platform built to ingest, store and analyze large volumes of varied security data without provisioning or maintaining data infrastructure. Data is kept in the open Parquet format, so teams do not have to trade coverage against cost, and security data and telemetry can be retained for up to 12 years. The design uses two tiers. The analytics tier is the existing Sentinel data layer for advanced hunting, alerting and incident management. The data lake tier provides long-term central storage for queries and Python-based analysis, with data from the analytics tier mirrored into it. Analysts can run KQL queries in an editor with IntelliSense, schedule jobs that promote results from the lake to the analytics tier, and use Jupyter notebooks for machine learning, visualization and scheduled runs. Activity auditing is enabled by default and records KQL access, notebook runs and job changes. All existing Sentinel data connectors are supported as sources, covering Microsoft Defender, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, firewall and network logs, and third-party identity logs. Typical uses are forensics, incident response and anomaly detection on historical data. The page does not name license requirements or prices.

minimal-apis.title: Minimal APIs overview – ASP.NET Core – Microsoft Learn
minimal-apis.notes: Minimal APIs are described as the recommended way to build fast HTTP APIs with ASP.NET Core. They let developers create complete REST endpoints with little code and configuration by declaring routes and actions fluently, which avoids traditional scaffolding and unnecessary controllers. Endpoints are registered with methods such as MapGet on the application object, and route values are bound to lambda parameters. The page lists simpler syntax, less boilerplate, lower overhead compared with controllers, easier testing and a modern approach as reasons to choose them for new projects, though it gives no benchmarks. The approach can be configured and customized to scale to several APIs, complex routes, authorization rules and control over response content. The page also names features that controller-based APIs offer out of the box but that Minimal APIs lack or need custom solutions for: extensible model binding through IModelBinderProvider and IModelBinder, advanced validation through IModelValidator, application parts or the application model, and OData support. Tutorials and a quick reference are linked for further guidance.

mlops.title: MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning – Microsoft Learn
mlops.notes: MLOps applies DevOps principles such as continuous integration, continuous delivery and continuous deployment to the lifecycle of machine learning models. Its aims are better quality and consistency of ML solutions, faster experimentation and model development, quicker deployment to production and stronger quality assurance with end-to-end lineage tracking. In Azure Machine Learning, reproducible pipelines chain steps like data preparation, feature extraction, hyperparameter tuning and evaluation, and reusable environments track pip and conda dependencies. Models are registered and versioned in a registry, identified by name and version. For production, a model is packaged as a Docker image and deployed to batch endpoints or online endpoints, with targets including managed online endpoints and Azure Kubernetes Service. Online endpoints support controlled rollout with several deployment versions, A/B testing and percentage-based traffic splitting. Job history, data asset tracking and interpretability support governance, while Azure Event Grid receives events such as run completion, model registration, deployment and data drift. Azure Pipelines can automate training and deployment. A registered model used in an active deployment cannot be deleted.
